text: INTERPRETER (lang-forms LF-3/LF-3b, parser desugar and checker diagnostics only): `for (a, b) in xs` (names and `_`, nested) now parses where it was an E0000 parse error; it desugars to the existing collection loop plus one field-access `let` per name, so every engine runs it as the hand-written desugar and the names are typed like `let (a, b) = p`. A pattern over a range and `for (a) in xs` stay parse errors. The generated statements of every collection `for` carry the `for` keyword's span and a `let (a, b)`'s lets the `let` span, so a diagnostic moves line (no new accept or refuse). `for x in d` over a Dict is still refused, now E0402 on the `for` line instead of E0102 on `len`. fmt prints both forms back. What an already-valid program computes is unchanged.
